strongest_angle: NASA completed a critical power-stretching operation on Voyager 1 by turning off three power-hungry devices simultaneously in September, followed by successfully resolving an unexpected 48-hour communication pause on October 20.

key_facts.fact: In September, NASA engineers completed a months-long effort to stretch Voyager 1's diminishing power supply by simultaneously turning off three power-hungry devices and substituting them with three lower-power alternatives.
On October 20, an unexpected loss of communication with Voyager 1 resolved itself autonomously after 48 hours before the NASA mission team could transmit diagnostic commands.

NASA's Deep Space Network was unable to detect a radio signal from Voyager 1 during two scheduled communication attempts on October 18 and October 19, when the spacecraft was located 16 billion miles (24 billion kilometers) from Earth.
